metrics.justification: No personal criminal or anti-corruption matter of record. The only personal litigation located is a defamation suit she brought as plaintiff (settled by a public apology in her favour, 2020), which is not an integrity matter against her; 2026 anti-corruption reports surfacing in searches name other former ministers, not her.

metrics.justification: Led the welfare response to the Global Ikhwan (GISB) child-abuse rescue (Sep 2024): welfare officers deployed and custody/care arranged for the 402 children rescued, with policy revisions following; she also moved on childcare-centre safety (mandatory CCTV from 1 Jan 2024, staff police screening) after abuse cases. Sustained, measurable response to a major flashpoint (anchor 3).

citation.title: Rescued children from GISB welfare homes receiving care and protection, says Nancy Shukri

metrics.justification: Made the Anti-Sexual Harassment Tribunal operational (regulations in force 8 Mar 2024, with a growing caseload) and enabled enforcement of the anti-stalking law (first charges from 2023); the Gender Equality Bill remained stalled amid opposition. Statutory mechanisms delivered and operative, one reform pending (anchor 3).

citation.title: 22 wins recorded at anti-sexual harassment tribunal

metrics.justification: Revised childcare and welfare-home registration and oversight policies after the GISB case (Nov 2024) and engaged the UN women's-rights treaty body (CEDAW, 2024). Institutional tightening prompted by crisis, with enforcement follow-through not yet documented (anchor 2).

On child marriage she stated candidly (20 Nov 2024) that the federal government opposes it but cannot impose a national ban because the matter sits under state and religious jurisdiction, naming the limited number of states that had amended their law. Honest framing of a constraint rather than a reversal of her own position (anchor 2).

citation.title: Ending child marriages in Malaysia an uphill battle, says Nancy Shukri
